protobuf-java-4.34.1.jar: CVE-2026-0994 is a false positive. The vulnerability is in the Python protobuf library's json_format.ParseDict() function — specifically a recursion-depth counter bug in Python's json_format.py. That code does not exist in the Java implementation. The NVD CPE cpe:/a:google:protobuf is language-agnostic and incorrectly matches the Java artifact. The fix versions cited (5.29.6, 6.33.5) are Python package versions; there is no corresponding Java fix because there is no vulnerability in the Java library. Added: 2026-04-23

httpcore-4.4.16.jar: CVE-2026-54399 and CVE-2026-54428 are false positives on the httpcore 4.x line. Both vulnerabilities are HTTP/2 issues in the HttpComponents Core 5.x codebase (the HPackDecoder / HTTP/2 header handling in httpcore5 / httpcore5-h2), fixed in 5.4.2. The httpcore 4.x line does not contain that HTTP/2 code and is not affected. The NVD CPE cpe:/a:apache:httpcomponents_core uses an upper-bound-only range ("up to and including 5.4.2"), so dependency-check numerically matches 4.4.16 (<= 5.4.2) on the shared CPE. 4.4.16 is the terminal 4.x release, so there is no newer 4.x to upgrade to; it is pulled in transitively by izgw-core's OCSP revocation code, which references only a couple of string constants from the 4.x jars. The 5.x artifacts (httpcore5/httpcore5-h2) already resolve to a fixed version (>= 5.4.3). Added: 2026-07-07

kotlin-stdlib-1.9.25.jar: CVE-2026-53914 is not exploitable in this service. The vulnerability is a BUILD-TIME issue in Kotlin's build cache metadata (unsafe deserialization, CWE-502), only reachable when compiling Kotlin with Kotlin's build tooling. izgw-transform is a Maven/Java service that runs no Kotlin compiler and no Kotlin build cache, so the vulnerable code path is not present at runtime. kotlin-stdlib is only on the classpath transitively (via okio/okhttp under org.hl7.fhir.utilities); a representative VXU^V04 -> FHIR conversion loaded 0 kotlin and 0 okhttp classes.
MATCH NOTE: kotlin-stdlib is a Gradle-built jar with no embedded META-INF/maven pom.properties, so the CI scan (dependency-check GitHub Action scanning the assembled fat jar) derives no Maven packageUrl for it and identifies it only by cpe:/a:jetbrains:kotlin. A packageUrl suppression therefore does not match; this rule matches by filePath (the nested jar filename), which works in both the fat-jar and Maven-plugin scans.
Scanner shows the inflated NVD 9.8 auto-score; JetBrains (CNA) rates it 6.7 Medium (AV:L/AC:H/PR:H). Fixed in Kotlin 2.4.20, not yet GA (betas only as of 2026-07-28). TEMPORARY: remove once Kotlin 2.4.20 GA is pinned via kotlin-bom in izgw-bom. Added: 2026-07-28 (IGDD-3141)

tomcat-embed-core: CVE-2026-66299 is a false positive for embedded Tomcat usage. The vulnerability is an unbounded buffer for undelivered messages in the WebSocket chat example web application bundled with the full Apache Tomcat distribution, allowing a slow client to exhaust memory. Apache's own advisory states users who removed the examples web application are not affected. Our use of tomcat-embed does not include the examples web application - this is Spring Boot's embedded Tomcat (tomcat-embed-core/-el/-websocket only, pulled in via izgw-bom's tomcat.version property), which never bundles the examples webapp in the first place. Confirmed as a known false-positive pattern on the Apache Tomcat security mailing list thread for this CVE.
MATCH NOTE: this CI job's dependency-check GitHub Action scans the assembled fat jar (--scan target/xform-*.jar) directly, which does not derive a resolvable Maven packageUrl for nested jars - the same root cause already documented in this file's kotlin-stdlib suppression below. A packageUrl-regex suppression therefore has zero matches here (confirmed in CI); matching by <sha1> of the exact jar works instead. SHA1 below is identical to the one already used in izgw-bom's own suppression file for this same CVE (same jar bytes, version-specific).
Fixed versions (11.0.25 / 10.1.58 / 9.0.121) had not been released as of this writing - confirmed tomcat-embed-core 10.1.58 does not yet exist on Maven Central (still under development). This entry is version-pinned (unlike the packageUrl approach) so it will need a new SHA1 once the tomcat.version property is bumped past 10.1.57 for any other reason - revisit once 10.1.58 ships either way. Added: 2026-08-08 (IGDD-3254)
tomcat-embed-websocket: see note on tomcat-embed-core CVE-2026-66299 above - same false positive, same fat-jar-scan packageUrl limitation, same fix. Added: 2026-08-08 (IGDD-3254)

CVE-2026-66908 is in the Apache Camel Platform HTTP Main component: the camel-main embedded HTTP server built JWTAuth from the keystore alone when neither jwtIssuer nor jwtAudience was set, so inbound tokens were checked only for signature and expiry (JWTAuthenticationConfigurer.buildJwtOptions, Vert.x JWTAuth). See CAMEL-24281.
That code is not on the classpath here. Verified on camel 4.18.4, in both the BOM validation tree and izgw-transform: - camel-platform-http-main : not resolved in either tree - io.vertx : not resolved in either tree - camel-main-4.18.4.jar : contains no JWT, platform-http or Vert.x classes izgw-transform is a Spring Boot application using camel-spring-boot-starter. It never starts camel-main's standalone HTTP server, and could not without Vert.x present. Dependency-Check matches on version alone: cpe:2.3:a:apache:camel:* covers "from 4.8.0 up to excluding 4.22.0" for every camel artifact, whatever the module.
There is no upgrade that clears this on our line. Per the advisory: "This behaviour is fixed only on 4.22.0 ... The fail-closed guard could not be backported. The jwtIssuer and jwtAudience options were themselves only introduced in 4.21.0 by CAMEL-23525, so on camel-4.18.x and camel-4.14.x there was nothing an operator could set to satisfy the requirement." 4.18.4 is the newest 4.18.x release, and camel 4.22.0 requires Spring Boot 4.1 / Spring Framework 7 while this BOM pins spring-boot.version on 3.5.x. The real remediation is the Spring Boot 4 plus Camel 4.22 upgrade. See versions-rules.xml for the cap that keeps automation on 4.18.x until then.
Matched on <cve> alone, with no dependency selector, so it applies wherever this one CVE is raised. Do not add <cpe>cpe:/a:apache:camel</cpe>: per the suppression XSD <cpe> is a suppress-what element, not a dependency selector, so it would hide every Camel finding including future ones.
WARNING - read before changing the date. This CVE is CVSS 7.5, at or above the --failOnCVSS 7 gate used by both dependency-updates.yml and publish.yml. When this suppression expires the scan fails hard: the nightly exits 1 with no PR, and publish.yml exits 1 so develop stops deploying to GitHub Packages. Recovery needs an edit to this file. The expiry is deliberate, to force the upgrade decision rather than let it drift, but it must be tracked so it does not land unattended. Expires 2027-02-28. Added: 2026-08-31

CVE-2026-59283 (SpEL SimpleEvaluationContext safety-guard bypass) and CVE-2026-59313 (functional-web SSE stream corruption): verified not exploitable in izgw-hub, izgw-transform, izgw-core, or v2tofhir — none use SimpleEvaluationContext for SpEL, and none use Spring's functional RouterFunction/HandlerFunction web framework for SSE. No fix exists on the Spring Framework 6.2.x line; the real fix ships only in 7.0.9, which requires Spring Boot 4.x. Should clear once the Boot 4 upgrade lands. Expires 2027-02-28. Added: 2026-09-02

CVE-2026-47892 (WebFlux.fn functional-endpoint header-predicate bypass) and CVE-2026-47893 (WebFlux HandshakeWebSocketService header leak): both require spring-webflux, which does not resolve on the classpath of izgw-hub, izgw-transform, izgw-core, or v2tofhir — verified independently in all four.
Flags on spring-core-6.2.19.jar despite webflux being absent because NVD tracks Spring Framework as one CPE product across all modules, not per-artifact — any module-specific CVE at this version matches every Spring jar we have, including spring-core. A Maven <exclusion> can't fix this: it's a version-string match, not a real transitive dependency, and spring-core itself is required by the framework regardless.
No fix exists on the Spring Framework 6.2.x line; the real fix ships only in 7.0.9, which requires Spring Boot 4.x. Should clear once the Boot 4 upgrade lands. Expires 2027-02-28. Added: 2026-09-02
